defects.summary: The status line says 'deviations 50–58, not yet reviewed', but the list runs to 59, and deviation 59 itself speaks of 'the fixes after the CR3 review', so the doc contradicts itself on the count and on the review state.
§0.2 names Opus as the builder of E5.5/E5.6, but the stories were built on Sonnet; deviation 59 records this honestly, but no operator has approved it.
The new TheVectorsCoverKimi test duplicates what the existing TheVectorsActuallyLoaded_AndCoverEveryPairOfTheTable already proves for kimi (the spec's S5.6.2), so it adds a redundant test.

The Scope/Scopes composite and the StandIn helper (WindowsStandIn + KimiCredentialsLock.RootFor + KimiSeams.Using) are copied into two new classes (here and AKimiQuestionRowTests) instead of reusing AKimiConsultationScenarioTests' identical helper.
TheFlags_AreD13s_..._NothingElseFlagged keeps its name now that kimi none/disk are admitted with the Unconfined flag, so the name is no longer true.
S5.5.1 checks only that --cwd contains 'own/tree', not that it is under the check's scratch root, which is weaker than the Then (it copies the existing Vibe test's shape).

summary: All twelve scenarios are present and pass; the planner arm (no flags; Snapshot with SnapshotSources for disk, Scratch for none), the refusal of any Leading/Flags in KimiConsultant, the three kimi rows with correct standings, cells and version 2.1.1, the vectors, the hand-written Runtimes list and the regenerated TS table all match E5.6's decisions, and the check and question-row tests prove junction-first one-shot disposal with real recorders that were given teeth. The findings are minor only: the deviation list's status and count disagree with each other, one test duplicates the existing S5.6.2 test, test helpers are copied, and the stories were built on Sonnet instead of the model §0.2 names (recorded honestly).
